outcome: Major congenital anomalies (overall and cardiac anomalies)
cohort: The study included 8,850,969 pregnancies (5,823,322 patients) from the French National Health Insurance Database between January 2012 and December 2023, identifying 408 pregnant individuals with osteogenesis imperfecta.
finding: Osteogenesis imperfecta was associated with increased risks of antepartum hemorrhage, chorioamnionitis, malpresentation, preterm delivery, and major congenital anomalies (especially cardiac anomalies), but no significant increase in postpartum fracture rates.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were notably higher in pregnant individuals with osteogenesis imperfecta compared to those without.
